title: Behavioral & Fresher Q&A
intro: Behavioral interview questions for Ruby freshers require answers that are honest, specific, and show genuine interest in the craft. This module covers the 60-second self-introduction for a junior Ruby developer (structure: who I am, what I've built, why Ruby, what I'm looking for), talking about college or bootcamp projects using the STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result — keep it under 2 minutes), answering why Ruby on Rails with an authentic response, the weakness question framed as an area of active growth with steps you are actually taking, handling questions you don't know the answer to (show curiosity — explain what you would do to find out), questions to ask the interviewer that signal genuine interest, how to stay current with Ruby and Rails (RubyWeekly, the Rails blog, reading gem source code), and the most common fresher interview mistakes to avoid.
